GEORGETOWN, MAY 10, 1859.


Mr. EDITOR.—The cross reminds me
that another year's subscription is about
to expire. I have been a constant reader
of the "Age" for more than nine years, and
have often been edified, not to say greatly
benefited by it, and cannot now give it up,
though I take half a dozen other papers.
I speak to some folks about taking paper,
and they say "I can't afford it"—but I can
not afford to be without one—aye more,
I commenced with one, then I wanted
two, and now take seven and "can't af-

ment of the readers of the Age; and whose

the "Giver of every good and perfect gift"?

twenty thousand readers?

What were, and are, "the persistent and malignant misrepresentations at the two extremes" of the Union, the North and South, which are here referred to? The official organ of the administration goes on to state them:

"It has been repeated," says the organ, "on every stump in the North, that it was the settled purpose of the slave States to force slavery into every State and Territory of the Union."
